candidate.educational_objective: Recognize and respond to an error-prone prohibited medication abbreviation.

options.A: Administer the dose because “U” is an approved abbreviation for units.
options.B: Clarify the order and have “units” written out because “U” is on the official Do Not Use list.
options.C: Interpret “U” as micrograms and administer the medication.
options.D: Change the order to “IU” because that abbreviation is preferred.

candidate.rationale: The Joint Commission’s official Do Not Use list includes “U” or “u” for units because it can be misread, including as a zero or another number. “IU” is also prohibited. The safer notation is to write the word “units” in full.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The abbreviation U/u for units is prohibited because it is error-prone; 'units' should be written out.
candidate.source_document_title: Official 'Do Not Use' List of Abbreviations / Standards FAQ IM.02.02.01
candidate.source_locator: IM.02.02.01 FAQ—minimum prohibited abbreviations include U/u and IU
candidate.stem: A medication order reads, “insulin lispro 6 U subcutaneously before lunch.” What should the nurse do?
